fatal_errors: The proposed machine-learning interatomic potentials are a simulation tool, not the experimental method used to produce a large-scale RHEA–Cu composite.
It omits liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
It does not identify preferential Ti removal from interdendritic channels, retention of the RHEA ligaments, or formation of the W-rich passivating interlayer.
No evidence is supplied that the proposed computational approach can cause or experimentally realize the claimed reaction and stable microstructure.
explanation: The response recognizes the general RHEA–Cu incompatibility problem but does not reconstruct the reported solution. The relevant method is liquid-metal dealloying: molten Cu selectively replaces Ti-rich interdendritic regions in directionally segregated WTaVTi, while W/Ta/V-rich regions remain as aligned RHEA ligaments. A spontaneously formed W-rich interfacial layer passivates the interface and helps arrest further exchange, enabling millimeter-scale reaction and a stable bicontinuous RHEA–Cu architecture. The generated hypothesis instead proposes an unsubstantiated computational optimization strategy, gives no matching processing conditions, and provides only a generic validation experiment with no quantitative observables or thresholds.
